speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It would not be an understatement to say that Singapore is like a small yacht in an open sea.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: When a sizeable cruise ship or oil tanker passes, we would feel the waves rather acutely.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The waves can come in the form of geopolitical tensions, economic instability, technological disruptions and environmental challenges.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Our diplomatic corps had never had it easy in their efforts to further Singapore's interests and, admittedly, things are only getting harder and harder.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: On one hand, our geographical limitations and natural resource constraints remain much the same as before.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, on the other hand, the world has become more volatile and less predictable, especially of late.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Misinformation and ideological echo chambers thrive, amplified by social media, contributing to polarisation of public opinion.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Nationalism, populist movements and extremist views take root more easily now more than ever, leading to societal divisions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The nature of contemporary threats, online and offline, tend to have transboundary impact and Singapore is not spared.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The world has not gotten any smaller physically, but it has gotten more tightly knitted with the advent of technology and social media.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Whether we like it or not, the impact of major global trends like climate change, sustainability, technological changes and threats to global governance and order remains a common challenge that affects all countries in the world today and requires multilateralism and a concerted global lens to solve.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: No one country can solve, through a singular unilateral policy, these problems on its back alone, for it requires a concerted effort together.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Even as we are on the topic of foreign policy, the terms "local" and "foreign" remain relevant insofar as making the distinction to refer to our collective identity as Singaporeans and as a people in wanting to protect our specific interests, our way of life, our cultures, our homeland and our sovereignty.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, in the context of addressing bigger challenges of the world that could directly impact our survival as a country, the local-foreign distinction needs to be fettered with a willingness to achieve outcomes and common good, building friendships across borders and being open to working together to achieve collective benefit, peace and security, whether it be in the region of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) or globally, in the context of the world today.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: To that end, my view is that Singapore owes it to our diplomats, past and present, who have dared to venture beyond our shores, representing us in faraway forums and lands to further our interests as a country.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It can sometimes be lonely, I am sure, and I begin this Adjournment Motion by thanking the work of our diplomats as Singapore's torchbearers on the global stage.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I am no diplomat but I have a care about how Singapore is positioned by others and how Singapore positions itself in the world today.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The first reason is that our citizens are now more exposed to the world more than ever.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Knowledge of the world is no longer just the remit of diplomats and a privileged few.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The world has changed over the last 20 to 30 years and information has been democratised to a wider base.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: With information readily available, citizens will form a view of Singapore's foreign policy, rightly or wrongly, and based on accurate information or otherwise.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: By this, I do not only mean Singaporeans based overseas but also to tap on the networks of Singaporeans based locally who have some reach, influence and awareness of other countries.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This could be in the form international networks amongst professionals, business owners, volunteers and students even, who, in themselves, take an open view of the world, venture out beyond our shores and let their personal or professional opportunities take them to new places.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: For our diplomatic efforts to be effective and to thrive, we must look beyond what governments can achieve from formal platforms alone and leverage on nurturing informal opportunities for meaningful relationships across peoples.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This layers further the nature and depth of connection among countries, allows the formation of closer ties that are first organic and most strongly felt at the level of our citizens and allows for policy-makers to have a nuanced awareness and understanding of the diversity, culture and worldview of others.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: With citizens at the base and as a foundation of our foreign policy, diplomatic efforts and trade opportunities would come more naturally and readily because it stems from a deep mutual appreciation of the other.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It must be that we are more proactive in articulating our ethos, values and principles as a country, how it is exercised inwardly through our education, housing and social policies and how it continues to be preserved and aligned outwardly in our foreign policy decisions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I argue that when decisions are based on our core values and principles and start from what we hold dear as a country, citizen engagement would actually be relatively straightforward and easy.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As a country, we already stand firm and unapologetically so on the importance of social cohesion in our neighbourhoods, on the expansion of common spaces to live together as a united people regardless of race, language or religion, and we value diversity along with the beauty and strength it brings us.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I would venture to further suggest that it is in our natural psyche and ability as Singaporeans to coexist with differences and differing viewpoints, to meet others in the middle to find practical solutions to global problems and then land on a principled and fair view even on something seemingly as complex as foreign policy and finding solutions to challenging global events of the day.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This is the only way possible for us to survive as a small city state and to advocate for a rules-based world order and for international law to flourish and take root.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We must remain open to building relationships, strengthen our existing friendships and build new ones and advocate for an even-handed, fair, just and principled approach to how we conduct ourselves and expect others to do the same as responsible citizens of the world.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Just like within family or a close-knitted friendship, we want everyone to succeed together, to do well and flourish and to live in peace and security.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is also only through a trusting relationship and friendship that we have the scope to be honest with one another and be candid about our views.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, the paradox is that our principles and values as well as the strength and closeness of our friendships are tested most when those close to us err in their actions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: No parent will relish calling the Police on their child who has erred in the eyes of the law and no true friend will find delight in reporting another's crime.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, when firmly grounded on sound principles and values, family and friends know this would be the right thing to do.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As part of our diplomatic efforts, our principles and values shine through not only by the side that we take, but also through the words we choose, as well as how and when we say them, right down to the pitch, the frequency and the volume of how we express them.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There is weight and gravity in the words and statements we make that belie the extent of the position or side we take on any given issue and we need to be sensitive to how that informs others of and aligns with our values and principles over issues.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Recently, in an CNA interview as part of his visit to Singapore, the hon United Nations (UN) Secretary-General Mr Antonio Guterres said, "We live in a situation in where practically there are no rules", describing the current state of affairs as a chaotic situation.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: He also highlighted a renewed need to "affirm the values" and that "without values everything is lost".

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: To hear this from the UN Secretary-General himself is both alarming sombre but perhaps somewhat reassuring at the same time.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It tells us of the disarray that the world is in today and how far the world is from the values we espouse to live by.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: But it offers a glimmer of hope for us to bolster and rally around multilateral organisations like the UN for a better world for ourselves and for others.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As part of being true to our principles and values, we must be ready, even as a small state, to express our views honestly with some candour and forthrightness, if necessary, even and especially to our closest allies and friends.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In the longer term, it makes for an honest friendship on the international stage where our viewpoints resonate with our citizens and matter to members of the global community, and this continues to put us in good standing as a country upholding values and principles.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It certainly is in our national interest to do so, yes, but more than most, we have the conviction and track record to show others that the world is better off when we have the will to cooperate and achieve consensus.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This perhaps has been a necessary function of our own painful lessons in history and our own limitations as a young nation.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: But we have shown that we are a people who thrive and continue to succeed only because we believe truly in a rules-based order and consensus building.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We also cannot afford to be passive about the quarrel of bigger others, simply because we will directly suffer the consequences of the uncertainty or escalation that could follow.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There is a Malay proverb, Mr Speaker, "Gajah sama gajah berjuang, pelanduk mati di tengah-tengah", loosely translated as "When two elephants collide or fight, it is the mousedeer in the middle that dies".

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In the context of a global order, we are the proverbial mousedeer that needs to be circumspect about how the elephants in the room are treating one another for our survival could depend on the extent to which things evolve between the stronger powers that be.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: We have also built goodwill and friendships not only with the bigger powers, but smaller states too know that we are a friend.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: My encouragement to the Ministry is to consider looking at the value Singapore can bring to the world and position ourselves as well-regarded partners for global benefit and progress.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I concede there are many layers to it and it would be impossible to unpack everything in all of 20 minutes.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Like many Singaporeans, I am concerned about Singapore's place in the world and how we navigate a less predictable future moving forward.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On behalf of all my colleagues at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA), I want to thank Dr Syed Harun for his contribution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, I agree completely with you and the thought did go through my mind that maybe I could just sit down and say it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The analogy you started off with was that Singapore is a yacht in a sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, think of a sampan in a typhoon.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are also witnessing deepening fractures in the global economy, ostensibly in the name of resilience and national security, but really due to a more fundamental lack of strategic trust between the superpowers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also see the continued erosion of global norms and global governance as the world makes this transition from a unipolar moment to a multipolar world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this has resulted in clearly, visibly inadequate responses to dealing with global challenges like climate change, pandemics and the challenges and risks of the digital revolution, the biotechnology revolution and the need for an energy transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Domestically, all over the world, we have seen the rise of xenophobia, hyper-nationalism, extremism and a bitter polarisation of domestic politics.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This, as you have said, is accelerated by misinformation and the social media echo chambers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew reminded us, "Singapore has to take the world as it is.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we can try to maximise the space we have to manoeuvre among the big trees".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our national interests and our vulnerabilities have remained unchanged all these decades.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are still a tiny, low-lying city-state in the middle of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The territorial seas of our neighbours enclose us completely.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our absence or our lack of a hinterland also remains an existential fact.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And that means Singapore needs to remain open as an existential need.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Or to put it more starkly, actually, nobody would care if Singapore disappeared under the waves overnight.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There are many other countries and ports that are queuing up to replace the functions that we currently perform.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to be more smart, more nimble, more organised, more reliable, more honest than anybody else.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Consequently, Singapore's foreign policy has several fundamental objectives to fulfil.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third, to expand economic opportunities for Singaporeans and to maintain our relevance to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And as a small state, I agree with you, we need to advocate for rules-based order with full respect for international law because without that, the risks for small states are exponentially high.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We try our best to shape global norms by making common cause with as many partners as possible on the basis of sovereign equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Dr Syed Harun has advised us to double-down on our values and principles.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I completely agree with you and that we need to speak up whenever and wherever there are transgressions of international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we do so consistently, even if that means, from time to time, having to say no to a superpower or to say no to a long-standing friend.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our consistent application of these principles has allowed us to maintain credibility with major and the middle powers and our neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Or put it another way, I say exactly the same thing in Beijing where I just came back from as I say in Washington, as I say in New Delhi or in Kuala Lumpur or Jakarta.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They know that it is based on a realistic assessment of Singapore's long-term strategic interests and our long-held principles and values.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They know that we are not acting on behalf of their rivals and they also know that Singapore cannot be bullied or bought.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, that makes my job easier because I can say the same thing everywhere and it does not have to be exactly identical to the positions taken by superpowers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the most important point you have made is that foreign policy begins at home and I completely agree with you.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Domestic unity, cohesion and consensus are essentially because without that, we cannot conduct effective foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I agree with you we do need to do far wider engagement of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We cannot treat foreign policy as something esoteric and elite.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is an exercise which every citizen, first, has a right to gain access to and understanding, and to participate in the discussion in the public space.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we also have to arrive at a common position because Singapore, being diverse and vulnerable, will always be exposed to foreign influence and way before hostility begins, influence operations to divide us, to create uncertainty, to erode our resolve would be conducted against us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The challenge that we have is we need to engage, we need to explain, we need to persuade, we need to mobilise and every Singaporean has to know why we take certain positions in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we need every Singaporean, wherever you live, work, study or travel, to also be our representatives – so, in a sense, we are all ambassadors now.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have already said that we are at risk of external forces dividing us and just look at the recent examples in the last couple of years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And those of you who accompanied me will know that I said the same thing in Jerusalem, in Ramallah, in Doha, in Cairo, in Abu Dhabi.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do need to recognise that there may be different interpretations of the origins of these conflicts or even the desired end-state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the point for Singapore is do not let that divide and erode our social harmony and cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Looking ahead, this House needs to be psychologically prepared that there was going to be more foreign policy issues in future which are sensitive, which are prickly and controversial and to recognise that Singaporeans will have different opinions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need to find consensus, we need find a middle ground and, as the Member said, we need to be able to express that credibly on the global stage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, I want to thank the Member again.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: His key points: foreign policy begins at home, that we need to be consistent overseas and that Singapore, with all our uniqueness, our diversity and our smallness, we can play an outsized role to make this world a little bit safer as we navigate the perilous storms in the next few years ahead.
